why: The wrapper's rules, its tests and its own proof (each file identical once whitespace is collapsed, nothing written unless every file passes) are spelled out, and the rest is running the script and adding three ignore files with exact contents. Only Markdown under docs and ripgrep's default search change; nothing at runtime reads these files, and a bad wrap is visible in the diff and reverted with one commit.
harm_if_wrong: A wrapped rule renders as a split list item or broken code span in a doc people and agents read, or a search silently skips a folder it should not, both easy to see and revert.
brief_problems: Commit 1's check expects --check to print 'docs/rules: 156', while the --check mode is described as printing 'only the current counts' in the format '<n> before, <n> after'; the exact line format of --check is left open.
The wrapper does not treat lines indented four spaces or more (indented code blocks) or HTML blocks as code; sameWords still proves no word changed, but their rendering could shift.
